# portable-pi

> A self-contained USB drive that runs the pi coding agent on Windows and Linux.
> No installation on the host machine. Sessions, credentials, skills and caches
> live on the drive. Repository: https://github.com/BalTac/portable-pi

## What it is

portable-pi builds a bootable-nothing, dependency-free USB stick (~430 MB) that
contains Node.js 24 LTS for Windows x64 and Linux x64, the `pi` coding agent
(pi-coding-agent 1.6.0, prebundled ESM), a configurable skill whitelist, and MinGit
for Windows so the agent's `bash` tool works even on a host without Git.
Plug it in, run `start.bat` (Windows) or `start.sh` (Linux), and the agent starts
with its own configuration, sessions and skills already in place.

## Isolation model

Isolation is configuration-level, not a sandbox:

- `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=<drive>/config/pi` — settings, extensions, packages,
  MCP servers, skills, sessions all live on the drive.
- `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1`, `PI_TELEMETRY=0`, temp and npm/node caches on the drive.
- the agent is launched as `pi -ns --skill <drive>/config/pi/skills`, which
  disables every discovered skill (including the host's `~/.agents/skills`) while
  keeping the drive's skills mounted.
- the agent still runs with the operating-system permissions of the user who
  started it; files outside the drive are reachable. For a real boundary, use a
  container, a VM or a dedicated guest account.

## Keywords

portable AI coding agent, USB flash drive, self-contained, no-install,
pi-coding-agent, agent skills, offline-capable CLI, Windows and Linux, x64,
exFAT, Node.js portable, MinGit, terminal agent, developer tooling,
reproducible agent environment, isolated agent configuration, LLM agent on a stick.

## Build and maintenance

- `scripts/build.ps1` (Windows) and `scripts/build.sh` (Linux) build a drive from
  `manifest.json`, which pins versions and lists included/excluded skills with reasons.
- `scripts/update.ps1` / `scripts/update.sh` refresh the runtime on an existing
  drive without touching credentials, sessions or user skills.
- `scripts/verify.ps1` / `scripts/verify.sh` assert the isolation guarantees and
  fail if anything is written outside the drive.

The public repository ships no skill names: the owner's whitelist lives in
`skills.local.json` (gitignored) and is merged into `<drive>/manifest.json` at build time.

## Provenance and license

MIT. Ideas and USB layout derived from `bnovik0v/portable-agent-usb` (MIT, 2026);
this is a rewrite for pi, not a git fork. See `NOTICE`.

## Files

- `manifest.json` — what gets built, with versions and the skill whitelist
- `README.md` — full documentation
- `docs/scope.md` — included/excluded skills and why
- `config/pi/AGENTS.md` — the instructions the agent reads on the drive
